Bourquin Exchange is the transit hub for that western and central cluster, and British Columbia Transit (BC Transit) route maps show routes 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 serving Bourquin Exchange.

The Central Abbotsford group is Horizon Place at 33233 Bourquin Crescent, Regency Park at 3150 Gladwin Road and its second tower at 3170 Gladwin Road, Alameda Court at 2277 McCallum Road, Mayfair Place at 33375 Mayfair Avenue, Cloud Croft Manor at 33464 George Ferguson Way, Parkside Place at 32640 Murray Avenue, Centennial Court at 2451 Gladwin Road and Lakewood Gardens at 2491 Gladwin Road.
Cascade Court at 35230 Delair Road is not a strata condo: it is a 55+ life lease residence in Abbotsford East, where a buyer acquires a lifetime right to occupy rather than a strata lot.

blocks.text: Abbotsford 55+ Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A 55+ condo here is governed by a strata age bylaw: Strata Property Act sections 123.1 and 123.2 permit a restriction to age 55 or older only, and any age bylaw below 55 — including older 45+ wording still found in stale building directories for Abbotsford towers — has been invalid since November 24, 2022.
Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs.

A life lease such as Cascade Court has no Form B, no depreciation report and no strata council: an up-front capital payment buys lifetime occupancy, monthly charges apply, and the operator redeems the lease on departure under its own terms, which vary by operator.

blocks.text: Abbotsford 55+ Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: BC Transit route 5 runs via Abbotsford Regional Hospital to Bourquin Exchange on the operator's route overview, which makes the hospital a named stop on the same system that serves the Old Yale Road condo cluster.

The City does not run the seniors housing in its inventory: eligibility and availability for assisted living and subsidized residences come from the operator or the health authority, not from the City of Abbotsford.

blocks.text: Abbotsford 55+ Condos: development and new projects

items.t: City-wide pipeline, from the City's Year 2 Housing Target Progress Report: since October 1, 2023 Abbotsford had approved rezoning, development permit and building permit applications amounting to 4,105 new housing units, of which 2,163 had building permits and may be under construction; status: council report dated November 4, 2025 (as of November 3, 2026). No project in that report is identified as a 55+ condo.

Abbotsford's Tax Rates Bylaw, 2026, No. 3727-2026 sets the Class 1 residential components per $1,000 of taxable value as general municipal (police) 1.08284, general municipal 1.78296, Fraser Valley Regional District library 0.08582, regional hospital 0.11583 and regional district 0.08836.

The same bylaw carries separate dyking and drainage taxes for the Matsqui Prairie and Sumas Prairie dyking districts — a line a lowland Abbotsford property can carry that an upland Mill Lake condo does not.

The City's Development and Amenity Cost Charge summary effective February 1, 2026 sets the total charge for an apartment dwelling unit at $20,423.00 — a new-build cost figure, not a charge on a resale condo.

BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley system centres Abbotsford bus service on Bourquin Exchange and Montrose Exchange, and its route map shows Bourquin Exchange served by routes 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6, with route 1 named Highstreet / University of the Fraser Valley (UFV).
Route 31 links Abbotsford to Mission Exchange and Mission City Station on BC Transit's route map — the intercity bus connection for a condo owner travelling north across the Fraser River.
Highway 1 (Trans-Canada Highway) runs across the north side of the city and Highway 11 runs south to the Huntingdon border crossing, both shown on the BC Transit system map for the city.

faq.a: They are in Abbotsford West and Central Abbotsford, not in Abbotsford East. The western cluster runs along Old Yale Road and Tims Avenue around Evergreen Village, Elmwood Manor and Royal Court, and the central cluster sits around Mill Lake on Gladwin Road, Bourquin Crescent and George Ferguson Way.
faq.q: Where in Abbotsford are the 55+ condos, in one sentence?

faq.a: No. Since November 24, 2022 the only age a British Columbia strata bylaw may set is 55 or older, and every 19+, 40+ or 45+ bylaw became invalid that day. Stale directory entries for Abbotsford buildings still showing a lower age are pre-2022 wording; the registered bylaw and the Form B for the specific unit are the documents that state the current rule.
faq.q: A directory calls a tower 45+. Can it still enforce that?

faq.a: A life lease buys occupancy, not title. The standard British Columbia model described by a life lease operator is an up-front capital payment for lifetime occupancy, monthly maintenance charges, and redemption by the operator on departure under the lease terms. There is no strata lot to resell on the open market, no Form B and no depreciation report, so the lease document itself is the due diligence.
faq.q: How is Cascade Court's life lease different from buying a condo?

faq.a: Whether a unit can be rented depends on the strata's current bylaws and the provincial rules that apply to them, and many 55+ buildings restrict rentals. Ask for the bylaws and the strata minutes before you buy a unit in Abbotsford as an investment.
faq.q: Can I rent out a 55+ unit in Abbotsford?

faq.a: Most 55+ strata communities in BC set an age rule in their bylaws, commonly that at least one resident is 55 or older, and many also limit children and rentals. The rules differ from one building to the next, so read the bylaws and the Form B Information Certificate before you make an offer on a unit in Abbotsford.
